title: Kinetic Criticality in Linker-Mediated Colloidal Aggregation
authors: Alexei V. Tkachenko, Soojung Lee, Zohar A. Arnon, Oleg Gang
abstract: Linker-mediated aggregation plays an important role in modern nanoscience. We demonstrate that it departs sharply from classical Smoluchowski kinetics because cluster reactivity evolves during growth. Combining theory with DNA-linked gold-nanoparticle experiments, we establish kinetic critical point controlled by linker abundance. Below threshold, active linkers are depleted and growth arrests; above threshold, clusters accumulate reactive sites, self-accelerate, and cross over to diffusion-limited coarsening. Experiments verify the predicted arrest, accelerated growth, and scaling collapse.
summary: This paper analyzes linker-mediated colloidal aggregation, showing that its kinetics are not classical but instead exhibit a sharp kinetic critical point. By controlling the linker concentration relative to this critical value, researchers can tune the system between an arrested state and one undergoing self-accelerating coarsening. This work provides a detailed model connecting chemical resource limitations to macroscopic changes in aggregation dynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates how linker-mediated colloidal aggregation deviates from classical Smoluchowski kinetics due to the dynamic evolution of cluster reactivity during growth.
main_result: The system exhibits a kinetic critical point controlled by linker abundance, leading to two distinct regimes: arrested growth below a critical linker concentration and self-accelerating coarsening above it.
method: The research combines theoretical modeling using rate equations with experimental validation employing DNA-linked gold nanoparticles measured via DLS.
model_or_system: The system involves colloidal particles linked by molecules, modeled by considering the interplay between diffusion and surface reactivity. The kinetics are governed by linker conservation laws leading to a critical point separating different aggregation fates.
key_observables: Hydrodynamic radii ($R_h$), cluster mass ($M$), and the existence/location of the kinetic critical point ($C^*_l$).
important_parameters: Linker concentration ($C_l$), critical linker concentration ($C^*_l$), and dimensionless time ($	au$).
main_assumptions: Initial linker adsorption is assumed to be nearly irreversible, and the system is analyzed using mean-field rate equations.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the kinetic critical point separating arrested growth (low $C_l$) from unlimited coarsening (high $C_l$), with DLS measurements confirming this separation in $R_h$ distributions over time.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the departure from classical kinetics, derives rate equations incorporating linker depletion, identifies the critical point mathematically, and validates these theoretical predictions using colloidal experiments.
why_interesting: While focused on colloids, the concept of a kinetic phase transition or bifurcation in reaction rates due to resource depletion (linkers) shares conceptual parallels with non-equilibrium dynamics studied in open quantum systems or complex chemical reactions.

FIG. 2. Kinetic criticality in linker-mediated colloidal aggre- gation. (a) DNA-functionalized nanoparticles bind through short single-stranded DNA linkers, forming interparticle bridges. (b) Free linkers first adsorb rapidly to particle surfaces, creating active binding sites, followed by linker- mediated cluster growth. (c) Below C∗ l = Cp/(1 −α), ac- tive linkers are exhausted and growth arrests at finite cluster size; above threshold, aggregation continues and crosses over to diffusion-limited coarsening.
